name: What happens between a Binance delisting announcement and removal

sections.hypothesis: Between a Binance spot delisting announcement and the coin's removal, its price either (a) keeps falling after the first day, so a holder should sell at once, or (b) rebounds from the forced selling, by more than costs. The study measures which, and how big the drop is, before any strategy.
sections.rationale: Who pays: holders who must leave before trading stops: users who won't withdraw to another exchange, funds and market makers that can't hold an unlisted coin. They sell into thinning liquidity within 2 to 14 days, and a buyer who can hold the coin elsewhere afterwards (withdrawals stay open for months) is paid a premium for taking it. That is the case for (b). The case for (a): the announcement reveals bad news (Binance cites weak development, volume, team commitment), and Binance's volume keeps leaving until the end. Outside evidence: equity index deletions show a price fall between announcement and the effective date, partly reversed after it (Lynch and Mendenhall 1997), but the reversal falls after the effective date, when Binance spot can't trade the coin; one earlier look at Monero's 2024 delisting found no rebound (Kestrel's to-do, Luke's idea 2026-11-14). Family: buying the fall is the reversal family, which the entry bar names as rejected; freezing this note is Luke's knowing override for (b). Outcome (a) is not a reversal and would be useful on its own: an exit rule for any strategy holding small coins (the basket strategies hold them). The short side (the fall itself) is recorded as information only: long-only spot can't take it (P5 parked). No delisted coin's prices were looked at before this note was written: the events come from kestrel ingest-delistings, announcements only.
sections.rules: kestrel delisting-study --research <this note> (kestrel.studies.delisting). Events: kestrel.data.delistings (Binance's announcements catalog, which starts 2022-02), coins whose removal is before 2025-11-01 00:00 UTC and that had a USDT market with daily bars; stablecoins and fiat tokens excluded; amended removal dates used (Gifto). 87 coins in 22 announcements expected. Daily bars (UTC). Day 0 is the UTC day of the announcement; the announcement comes out during day 0 (03:00 to 10:00 UTC), so the earliest realistic trade is day 1's open. Removal day R is the UTC day trading stops (03:00 or 09:00 UTC): its open, 00:00 UTC, is the last price a holder can surely trade at. Per coin, log returns: pre-drift, close of day -31 to close of day -1; announcement day, close of day -1 to close of day 0; the window, open of day 1 to open of day R. Each is also shown market-adjusted (minus BTCUSDT's log return over the same span). The trade tested: buy at day 1's open, sell at day R's open. Coins announced together share a date, so each announcement's coins are averaged first (equal weight) and the announcement is the unit: 22 events, bootstrapped by announcement. A coin missing a needed bar is reported; if its bars stop before day R, the last close is the exit and it is flagged, not dropped.
sections.falsification: Each coin's cost C is its round trip (costs below); each announcement's is the mean of its coins'. (b) REBOUND: PROCEED to a strategy note only if the mean over announcements of (window - 2C) is above 0 with a bootstrap P(> 0) of at least 90%, and the window's mean net of BTC is above 0 (not just a rising market). That is, it survives twice the cost (scorecard rule 5). (a) EXIT RULE: PROCEED to an exit-rule note only if the mean window is below -2C (mean C over announcements) with P(mean < 0) at least 90%: selling at day 1's open beats holding to removal by more than twice the cost. Otherwise KILL, and no strategy or rule is built from it. Run once; the descriptive figures (pre-drift, announcement day, the short side) are reported whatever the verdict and decide nothing.
sections.parameters: Fixed before looking: day 1 open entry, day R open exit, 30-day pre-drift, BTCUSDT as the market, equal weight within an announcement, 5,000 bootstrap resamples over announcements, seed fixed. No other entry day, window or filter is tried; any change is a new version with a reason, and its run counts. No holdout data: every bar used is before 2025-11-01 (the 2025-10-29 announcement, removed 2025-11-12, is out).
sections.costs: One round trip per coin: taker fee 7.5 bps a side and the coin's half-spread from its volume tier in kestrel.toml at the announcement (delisted coins are almost all in the 15 bps tier): about 0.45% round trip, so 2C is about 0.90%. Spreads widen as removal nears, so the real cost is likely higher: the report also shows the window less 3x the cost. Impact at 330 USDT is negligible. A study, not a strategy run: one look, logged in the findings.

history.reason: Study passed with the pre-registered EXIT RULE verdict (2026-11-15). Whether to write an exit-rule note is open in TODO.md.
